segments.text: People think SVM is just a line. But it is actually a hyperplane in high-dimensional space.
Let me explain the kernel trick. When data is not linearly separable in 2D, we map it to higher dimensions.
The support vectors are the closest points to the hyperplane. They define the margin.
Now let me talk about something completely different. Yesterday I went to the grocery store.
The regularization parameter C controls the trade-off between margin size and misclassification.
For non-linear problems, we use the RBF kernel. It maps inputs to infinite-dimensional space.
In summary, SVM finds the optimal hyperplane by maximizing the margin between support vectors.
